Subject: Follow-up: Model routing & policy configuration (post-discovery)

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move toward a technical proof-of-concept: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use case: customer support chat widget + internal knowledge base reranking for search.
- Traffic: ~350 reqs/min at peak, median request size 400 tokens.
- Latency targets: p95 < 200ms for primary chat route; best-effort for background rerank/embeddings.
- Data residency: must keep EU customer data in EU for EU customers; global for others.

Key technical asks we discussed to validate in POC:
1) SDK & auth: quickstart for our JS/py SDK and API-key provisioning + optional VPC/private deployment.
2) Routing & policy: per-route policies by latency/cost (e.g., prefer low-latency GPU-backed model for chat, fallback to quantized model when capacity constrained).
3) Structured output / tool calling: we need deterministic JSON outputs for actions (ticket creation).
4) Embeddings + rerankers: hybrid approach — server-side embeddings + on-the-fly rerank to improve precision.

Attached is a rough example routing config (redwood-model-routing-examples.yaml) that illustrates the fallback chain and region routing we talked through.

Proposed next steps:
- Dev to share a short POC plan with config + estimate (Dev/Marcus) — target EOD Friday.
- We’ll schedule a 60-min architecture sync next week to walk through the config and auth steps (Tom + Security).
- I’ll loop procurement separately on contract/timeline.

Would love confirmation from you on the latency SLOs above and any additional compliance needs.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model routing & policy configuration (technical details)

Hi Tom —

Great to meet you on the call. A few quick technical notes that map to the POC and the example YAML I attached earlier: 

1) SDK & auth:
- SDKs (JS + Python) use API keys by default. For POC we can issue scoped API keys tied to the Acme account.
- For Private/VPC deployments we support token-exchange with your IdP and KMS integration; we’ll provide a runbook.

2) Routing & policy (example):
- Route "chat-primary":
  - preferred_model: redwood-chat-lx (GPU, low-latency)
  - p95_target_ms: "200"
  - fallback_chain: [redwood-chat-lx-quant, redwood-chat-slim]
  - region_routing: request.metadata.region || "us-west-2"

- Route "search-rerank":
  - preferred_model: redwood-embed-xx
  - batching: true (batch window 50ms)
  - priority: background
  - cost_policy: prefer-quantized-if-cost>THRESHOLD

3) Structured output/tool calling:
- We support function/tool-calling with enforced schemas. For deterministic ticket creation, we recommend using the structured-output mode with a strict JSON schema; SDK will validate before forwarding.

4) Embeddings + reranker:
- Store customer embeddings in your vector DB; Redwood produces embeddings and supports a server-side rerank step to reduce round trips.

Next steps I’ll take:
- Produce a one-page POC config (YAML) tuned to your traffic and latency targets.
- Include a minimal quickstart (API key, sample request, SDK snippet) and a short checklist for your security team.

Marissa — I’ll have that POC package by EOD Friday.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Naomi — can you prep a SOC2 packet and a one-slide VPC diagram? Marcus — can you size the expected GPU footprint for the POC (2-week run) so we can give cost guidance?

I’ll send the consolidated package to Tom once we have the POC YAML + security artifacts.
